text:
maya: Noticed a weird case with streaming and auth refresh: when the auth token refreshes mid-stream we sometimes reconnect and the client emits a duplicate final fragment. Wanted to surface and check parity fixes. :confused:
theo: Do you have a small repro? Is this happening with long-poll reconnects or SSE-only?
maya: SSE only. Flow: server sends partial JSON (no trailing newline), client sees socket close due to token expiry, client reconnects and server replays last event. Our parser emits the partial on close then again after reconnect when the replayed chunk completes.
ryan: Oof. So two issues: 1) partial fragment emitted on close, 2) server replaying last event on reconnect. Combined they cause duplicates rather than loss.
zara: Which SDKs show this? Node, browser, Python?
maya: Hit in browser and node. Python's generator-based iterator tended to suppress duplicates because it buffers until a full JSON object; Node's line-based SSE parser will flush on 'close' and then again when the replay arrives.
theo: Quick idea: attach a per-chunk monotonic id if available in events (e.g., event-id header or server-assigned seq). If not present, we can use a weak dedupe window: keep hash of last N emitted fragments and drop exact duplicates within 5s. That should be opt-in, though.
ryan: I think opt-in is good. We can't force servers to add ids for all models. Plus hashing helps when replayed payloads are identical.
maya: For immediate workaround, apps can call sdk.stream(...).suppressDuplicates(true) which will enable a small LRU dedupe cache. We don't have that API yet though.
sync-bot: CI: found failing test sse_reconnect_dupes in nightly suite. Link: https://ci.internal/9876 :rotating_light:

theo: Proposed patch: 1) change parser.closeHandler to attempt a non-blocking parse of remaining buffer but mark those fragments as provisional, 2) when a new stream reconnects within X ms and emits an item identical to a provisional fragment, drop the duplicate and promote the provisional to final if still present. 3) expose sdk.stream({ dedupe_window_ms }) and docs.

zara: Sounds reasonable. Edge-case: what if provisional fragment is incomplete and the replay completes it with more data that legitimately extends the text? Hashing full string would treat them as different; need to only dedupe exact duplicates. So we must not dedupe prefixes.

theo: Agree. We'll only dedupe complete JSON objects. For incomplete fragments we parse them as provisional but never emit until they're complete or the stream definitively terminated. Emitting incomplete fragments seems dangerous unless apps explicitly opt-in to receive partial tokens.

maya: That mirrors Python behavior and would make parity clearer. We should update the SDK parity matrix and add a sample app under examples/streaming-dedupe that demonstrates token rotation mid-stream and how to handle it.

ryan: Tests: unit tests for parser with mixed split-chunk inputs, integration test with auth refresh (simulate server 401 then reconnect + replay), and e2e in browser harness. Also add a migration note: consumers on older SDKs who relied on flush-on-close will now need to opt into partial emission with .emitPartial(true).

sync-bot: Ticket created: DX-4122 "sse: dedupe/rewrite parser behavior on reconnect + auth-refresh" assigned to @theo.

zara: I'll help with the browser harness. Maya, can you paste the minimal server sequence you used?
maya: Sure: sequence of server writes (each followed by flush): 1) data: {"chunk":"hello","seq":5}
2) data: {"chunk":" world","seq":6} but split bytewise so second write is "data: {\"chunk\": \" wor" then after 60ms "ld\",\"seq\":6}
3) close connection with 401 to force client refresh and reconnect. On reconnect server replays event seq 6 fully.

theo: Perfect. I'll implement parser changes and add tests. Plan: draft PR today, land behind feature flag, enable by default after one week of canary.

maya: Thanks. This will reduce duplicate tokens for folks hitting token rotation windows. Also let's add a short note in onboarding docs about token TTLs and recommend graceful refresh strategies.

ryan: +1. Document sample code for debounce+dedupe in the Node/Browser SDK READMEs.
